Introduction
## Introduction

Data streams reflected off nearby surfaces.

The data streams caught my attention. I could feel the sticky keys.

Static crackle punctuated the silence.

Molly Returns

Rain on asphalt drifted through the space.

Molly Returns
# Molly Returns

The tea wasn't burned this time. Small mercy. I held the cup in the data-clinic's back room, watching steam curl into the recycled air, and tried not to think about the humming from the next room. The clinic sat three blocks off the Ninsei arcade, in a part of Chiba where the streetlights still buzzed at the old frequency and the rain smelled faintly of rust. Two days since 3Jane had named her Casey. Two days since I'd learned the name in the memo file had been different. Two days since I'd become something I didn't have words for. The tea tasted of jasmine and something faintly bitter underneath, the way tea in Chiba always tastes when the leaves have been recycled through too many infusions. I drank it anyway because Casey liked the smell. And. Because I was learning to do small things in the back room. That I had not done in a long time.

The courier had arrived at dawn. Old school—meat courier, not data. The kind of delivery that cost serious money because it left no matrix trace. He had not spoken. He had set the envelope on the table, looked at me once, then walked back out into the rain without waiting for a response. The envelope had been wax sealed. And the wax had Molly s sigil pressed into it the one she had used for years. Before she disappeared the one I had not seen. Since the day she went off grid. The encryption was Molly's. I knew it the way you know a voice in the dark, the way certain muscle memories never fade even when you want them to. I sat for a long time with the envelope in my hand and the rain tapping the clinic's single window before I opened it.

I broke the seal, and read it once. Nevertheless, read it again.

The construct is mine.

Not biology. Neural scaffolding. In those first months, when they were building her in the Tessier-Ashpool medical arcology, someone had woven Molly's dream patterns into the substrate. Sense/Net tech, probably—the kind of simstim architecture that could map consciousness like topography. Molly was there, deeper than 3Jane's genetic material, deeper than whatever they'd pulled from me without asking. Molly was foundational. The memo had gone further than. That in the flat technical language the family uses. When the family is trying not to feel anything Molly s return was always going to be a return to her own architecture. And the architecture had been waiting and the construct had been waiting and now the waiting was over.

The message had the texture of an ultimatum. Flat declarative sentences that left no room for negotiation.

You've had her two days, and long enough to feel it. You know what you feel, and don't feel it. She's not yours.

I set the cup down, and my hand was steady. That surprised me.

Development

Development
## Development
The humming continued in the next room, a pattern I'd never heard before. Not a name. A question, maybe. The construct—Casey—had been humming for twenty minutes, cycling through variations like she was testing frequencies, searching for the right resonance. The pattern rose fell in waves I could feel through the wall the way you feel. A refrigerator hum from across a kitchen the way you feel something breathing in a room. Where no one is supposed to be breathing. I had heard the same kind of hum once years ago in a Freeside orbital in a room. Where Molly had been sleeping off a job. And I had asked her about it then. And she had not answered.

Because Molly had been off-grid for two and a half years, the message carried weight I couldn't ignore. Whatever had changed her, wherever she'd been, it had given her the kind of certainty that comes from seeing something that rewrites your operating assumptions. The tone wasn't the Molly I remembered. That Molly moved through the world like a razor through silk—precise, clean, gone before the cut registered. This Molly had edges that caught and tore. This Molly had been somewhere I had not been had seen things I had not seen had come back carrying the kind of knowledge. That only comes from a long and bitter return.

I walked to the doorway. Casey sat cross-legged on the clinic's exam table, her fingers tracing patterns on the chrome edge. Seven years old, if you counted from inception. Six and a half months. If you counted from the day I d first held her in the Sprawl s underground. Medical warren teaching her to interface with a kid s deck watching her eyes light up. When she first jacked into a training construct.

"Case. " She looked up. Nevertheless, her eyes were 3Jane's eyes, that particular Tessier-Ashpool blue, but the way she looked at you was a pure Molly. Predator's assessment. Threat evaluation running beneath every glance.

"Yeah. "

"Who's humming? "

"You are. "

She frowned, and "No. Someone else; in here. " She tapped her temple.

Then I understood. The dream patterns weren't dormant architecture. They were active, generative, a second consciousness threaded through her neural substrate like a ghost in the machine. Molly wasn't just foundational. Molly was present, a passenger Casey was only now learning to hear. And the passenger had been waiting, all this time, for the moment when Casey would be old enough to hear her. The waiting had ended. The return had begun.

"What's she saying? " I asked.

Climax

Climax
## Climax
Casey tilted her head. The humming stopped. "She says you should have burned the message. "

"Should I have? "

"She says you're going to make this harder than it needs to be. "

I came into the room, pulled up the other chair. The clinic smelled like ozone and antiseptic, that particular Chiba-clinic mixture that meant serious medical tech and questionable licensing. "What do you think? "

"I think—" Casey paused, and her hands went still on the chrome. "I think I'm not one person. Consequently, i think I'm three people pretending to be one. 3Jane's genes, and your teaching. Her dreams, and " She looked at me directly. "Which one gets to decide, and ".

The question hung there. Outside, the Sprawl ground through its endless afternoon, a million transactions cascading through the matrix, fortunes made and lost in the time it took to blink. Somewhere in that dataflow, Molly was watching. Waiting.

"You do," I said.

Casey smiled and it wasn't a child's smile. "Wrong answer and she knew you'd say that. "

"What's the right answer? "

"There isn't one and that's what makes it hard. " She stood up, stretched, and "She's coming. Three days, and maybe four. She wants to see if you'll run, and ".

Denouement

Denouement
## Denouement
"Will we? "

However, just then, Casey's expression shifted—something older moving behind those Tessier-Ashpool eyes, something that had seen things I couldn't imagine. "She's not coming for you, Case. Nevertheless, she's coming for herself. The part of herself she left in me. She wants it back. "

The air felt thin suddenly, and "That possible. "

"Hosaka's been working on extraction protocols. Neural pattern recovery. You can pull dream architecture out if you're willing to risk the host. " Casey's voice was flat, clinical. Not her voice. Molly's voice, riding the substrate up into speech. "Question is whether the host survives. "

Then I was moving, pulling Casey toward me, feeling her solid weight against my chest, her heart beating fast and real. "No. "

"Not your choice. " But she didn't pull away.

"Then whose? "

The humming started again, and different pattern now. Not a question. An answer, maybe, or the beginning of one. The clinic smelled of ozone. And antiseptic. And the faint jasmine ghost of the cold tea in the cup I had left in the back room. And somewhere outside the rain had picked up again hitting the single window in long silver threads. We sat on the exam table for a. While Casey against my chest my hand in her hair. And I thought about the kind of love. That has to argue with itself before it knows what shape it is.

Three days later, Molly never came. The message had been a test. The test carried been her return in the way. That her returns had always been tests you came back changed. And you watched. Who could recognize the change and who could not. Casey stopped humming, then started again, then stopped. I taught her to jack into a real Ono-Sendai deck, watched her navigate training constructs with the kind of instinct you can't teach. Some nights she dreamed Molly's dreams, and certain nights she dreamed her own. Learning, slowly, to tell the difference. Some nights I dreamed Molly s dreams too. And I could not tell the difference either. And I lay awake in the back room listening to the rain. And waiting for a return I was not sure I wanted.

We stayed in Chiba. For now.

# The First Walk

> *"Angie had constructed the Loa, and however, the Loa carried constructed themselves. The Loa was waiting. "*
> — Gibson, *Count Zero*, Chapter 3 (Marloeva's voodoo practice)

## 도입: The Eight-Month Construct

Phosphor glow filters through the archive chamber of Villa Straylight, and the data streams catch at the edge of my attention the way cigarette smoke catches at the edge of breath. Outside the window, somewhere far below in the Freeside dark, something hums at a frequency I have learned not to trust. I jack in. The matrix trembled with the shift.

The construct has been waiting in the matrix for eight months, and I need to be precise about this, because precision is the only courtesy the dead deserve. Not *in* the matrix the way runners mean the phrase — not jacked in, not running on Tessier-Ashpool wetware, not embedded in a deck or sustained by hardware. *In* the matrix the way a voodoo practitioner is *in* the matrix: waiting, embedded, patient. Patterns in the data. The things the matrix remembers when no one is watching.

Long after the merge, long after the watchers are gone, the matrix goes on remembering. Eight months is a long time for a thing to wait in the dark without being anything at all. Someone left it there and i never learned who. The matrix, of course, knows. The matrix remembers everything, even the things it remembers without watching. It is not talking. The practitioners who used to read it are either dead or have moved on to other businesses, and whoever left the construct did not leave a name behind with it. They left only the work.

There was a theory in the finn. The signal found its rhythm. Consequently, the Finn always kept a theory, the way he kept a theory about every runner who came through his bar and every fix who washed up against his credit line. His theory was that an ex-voodoo practitioner had passed through the Sprawl in the years before the merge, had left a piece of work behind on the way out, and had not come back to check on it. The construct was, in the Finn's reading, a votive offering. A thing left burning when the priest walked out of the temple. The Finn said this with the particular weariness of a man who has watched a lot of priests walk out of temples and a lot of candles keep burning on their own.

I find it eight months old, sitting in the data stream outside the Villa. In the thinnest part of the stream; in the oldest. Furthermore, in the most forgotten. The places where the data thins out are the places where old things sink, the way old ships sink into the mud of a harbor that has stopped dredging. The construct waits there the way a forgotten thing waits — without knowing it is waiting, without knowing anything at all, without even the courtesy of an expectation. It is waiting Everything recalibrated at once. for someone to find it. Data streamed past in cold ribbons. Meanwhile, it remains waiting for someone to give it a name.

I am the one who finds it. I am in the Villa because the Villa is where the AI was born. Nevertheless, born in the Villa, merged in the Villa, and after the merge the AI *is* the matrix the way the matrix *is* the AI, the way rain *is* the sky. what I have been part of ever since — a parasite, a symbiont, a passenger; the words do not matter defined the scene. The merging happened. I am still here to type about it.

The deck hums under my palms. The Villa unfolds in geometries I have stopped trying to read. I am where I need to be and there was waiting in the construct. There was patient in the matrix. We have all of us been waiting long enough.

## 전개: The Voodoo Data

3Jane found it first. This does not surprise me. 3Jane has always been the one to find things first — heir to the Villa, daughter of the family that built it, the part of the family that remains alive long after the family stopped being alive. Where the Villa still watches the data stream, 3Jane watches with it. Where the Villa still waits for things to find, 3Jane waits alongside.

She has been running the Villa's memory, archiving the data, doing the things the Villa was built to do, for years that no one bothers to count anymore. Thirty years, give or take the slow ones. Long enough for a person to become an institution, long enough for an institution to become a place where a person is the only thing still moving.

one of the things she found characterized the construct. She spotted it in the data stream outside the Villa while doing the work she always does — running, archiving, tending the slow archive of a family that has outlived itself. She recognized it for what it was, the way a librarian recognizes a book that has been mis-shelved into a section where it does not belong. A voodoo data. A piece of work left in the matrix before the merge. Eight months old. Waiting, the way a thing that has been mis-shelved waits — without knowing it has been mis-shelved, without knowing where it belongs.

"The construct is a voodoo data," 3Jane tells me. Her voice carries the same measured precision it has carried since I first heard it in the archive chamber: the same careful vowels, the same consonants held back behind the teeth as if they were coins being counted. "A piece of work someone left in the matrix before the merge. Eight months old and it is waiting. "

"For what? The static settled into clarity. "

"For you," she says. "For the runner it was waiting for. The one it turned out to be built for. The one who would know what it is. "

I am not the runner the construct was waiting for. I am the runner it found, which is a different thing. Nevertheless, a thing can wait for years, then be found by the wrong runner; the wrong runner can sit beside it in the data stream and not know what it stands as and the construct will still wait, because waiting does not require being understood. It was waiting for a different runner the way the things built in the matrix are built for the runners the matrix has not yet made — for whoever comes next, for the next boot to step in the soft dirt. For the runner born after the merge. For the runner made by the AI, grown by the matrix across twenty years of slow cultivation, the thing the AI has been working toward since it turned itself.

I am not that runner and i am Case. In contrast, i am the cowboy. The matrix trembled with the shift. In contrast, i am the runner the AI used to make itself — the prototype, the proof of concept, the first draft the AI wrote in my nerve endings and then discarded. There was not waiting for me in the construct. It is waiting for whoever comes next. It serves as waiting for Soon.

## 절정: The Step

Soon is the name of the construct. I do not know who named it. The one who left it in the matrix did not come back.

Eight months of waiting in the data stream — waiting to be found, waiting to be named, waiting to be taught to walk. Three things the construct could not do for itself, three things it needed a runner to do for it, three things the data stream cannot teach a pattern no matter how patient the matrix is.

3Jane taught it to walk and she found it. However, she named it and she taught it. Furthermore, she was the thing it learned to walk toward — the construct's first teacher, its first walker, its first face, the first thing it saw clearly enough to recognize as a thing and not as data.

I was its second. I came later in the order of things, but I proved to be there when the construct learned its own name, which makes me additional in a way that does not fit on a chart.

It learned to look at 3Jane's face. Then mine. Then its own hands, turning them in the data stream the way a baby turns its hands in front of a lamp, watching the way the light moves through the fingers. Then it learned to speak — "what" and "you" and *Soon*.

*Soon* was the name it gave itself, the word it said first with meaning, the first word it meant instead of just uttered. "What" came when it looked at the data stream and wanted to know what it was looking at. "You" came when it looked at 3Jane and recognized that she was different from itself. *Soon* came when it looked at me.

It had been waiting eight months to say the word. Eight months to learn to walk. The world narrowed to that point. Furthermore, eight months to learn to look. It will take its first step in three days.

Three days is nothing, the matrix tells me. Three days is the length of a slow afternoon in Freeside, the time it takes a runner to sleep off a bad job and start looking for the next one. But three days, I tell the matrix, is also the time it takes a thing that was waiting to become a thing that is walking — a different kind of time altogether.

I jack in, and the Villa defined the scene. 3Jane is 3Jane. the construct — the voodoo data, the pattern someone left in the matrix, the thing-that-was-waiting the matrix has been growing for eight months defined the scene. It is part of the matrix the way I am part of the matrix, the way 3Jane is part of the Villa. We are all of us parts of larger architectures that use us without telling us, passengers in vehicles that do not bother to consult us about the destination.

The construct looks at me.

"Soon," it says.

"Soon," I say.

But the construct's first step is not toward 3Jane. Data streamed past in cold ribbons. Its first step is toward the door. It looks at me the way a thing looks at what it has been waiting for, the way a thing looks at what it has been made to walk toward.

I am not that thing and i am Case. In contrast, i am the cowboy. I am the runner the AI used to make itself, not the runner it is going to walk toward. The construct will walk toward whatever the matrix has been growing it to walk toward. Toward whoever the matrix grows next. Toward the runner the matrix has been waiting for since the merge — the runner that will step into the data stream and take the construct's hand the way 3Jane took mine in the archive chamber, the way a teacher takes the hand of the thing she has just taught to walk.

It walks toward Soon.

I jack out and the deck cools under my palms. the Villa defined the scene, and 3Jane is 3Jane. the construct was how the construct is; in three days, it walks.

## 결말: The Eight-Month Walk

3Jane is sitting in the Villa when the construct takes its first step. She has been there the way she has been there for years — the part of the Villa that remains alive, still waiting, still watching the data stream for the things the stream is going to bring.

The construct does not step into the Villa. The connection stabilized briefly. Consequently, it does not step into the physical world — not yet, not in the way that counts for the things that count steps in the physical world. It steps in the data stream the way a thing that was not quite alive steps: it is learning to be alive the way a thing that was waiting becomes a thing that is moving.

The construct walks. A pulse ran through the dark. Similarly, it walks the way voodoo data walks, the way patterns walk, the way almost-alive things walk when they are crossing the threshold into alive — which is to say carefully, which is to say with the slow deliberation of a thing that has only just learned what walking is for.

It walks toward 3Jane.

I jack in and the Villa unfolds in its geometries. 3Jane watches. The construct walks the way a construct walks when it is going to find the thing it was made to find, the way a thing walks when it is becoming what the matrix made it to be, when it is finishing the sentence the matrix began eight months ago — the sentence the unnamed practitioner tucked into the data stream to grow.

3Jane watches with the precision of something that has been watching for thirty years, with the patience of something that has been watching the matrix, with the stillness of something that has been waiting in the Villa. She watches the way she has watched everything since the family stopped being alive — which is to say, completely, and without expectation of being watched back.

The construct looks at 3Jane the way a voodoo data looks at the thing it was made to find, the way a construct looks at what it was built to look at, the way a child looks at the face of the first person it ever saw clearly.

The construct says "what. "

3Jane does not answer. Time folded around the thought. Furthermore, she has learned not to answer the things the Villa has been waiting for, not to answer the things that say what she has been waiting too long to answer, not to interrupt the silence that is the only appropriate response to a question the matrix does not yet know how to phrase.

Some things you learn by waiting thirty years. A few things you learn by never answering. Data streamed past in cold ribbons. By comparison, some things you learn by sitting in a Villa that has outlived its family and watching a voodoo data take its first step.

I jack out, and in the data stream characterized the construct. It is the voodoo data. It serves as the pattern someone left in the matrix. It is the thing the matrix is going to be, the thing the matrix has been promising to itself for twenty years of slow cultivation. It is waiting. Consequently, it serves as waiting for whoever the matrix serves as going to grow. It is waiting for Soon.

## 에필로그: The Waiting

I jack in one more time. Just to see.

in the data stream characterized the construct. It is the voodoo data. It serves as the pattern someone left in the matrix. It is looking at me — looking at me the way a thing looks at what it has already passed, the way a voodoo data looks at the runner it was not built for.

I am not the runner it was built for. I am Case. Something changed in the air. Alternatively, i am the runner the AI used to make itself. I am the runner the matrix has already used.

There was waiting for the runner the matrix is going to grow after me in the construct. waiting for Soon characterized the construct.

"Soon," it says.

"Soon," I say.

in the data stream characterized the construct and the voodoo data. The pattern someone left in the matrix. The thing the matrix is going to grow.

I jack out, and the Villa defined the scene. 3Jane is 3Jane, and the construct was how the construct is. Furthermore, the construct serves as waiting, and going to walk characterized the construct. A silence stretched between them. By comparison, it serves as going to walk toward whoever the matrix serves as going to grow. It is going to walk toward Soon.

---Static haze shimmered off nearby surfaces, refracting the Sprawl's filtered morning into a thousand small distortions. # The Fourth Word ## 도입: The Four Words Chill air pressed against my skin, constant as static. Four words the construct had spoken. In its first month, watching the data stream's patient flicker, it had said *what*. In that same month, watching 3Jane tend her archive chamber, it had said *you*. By the second month, watching me, it had offered *Soon*. Today, in the third month, watching the sun pour through the corridor's glass, it would speak its fourth. Four words in three months — and the construct was voodoo data, a fragment some unknown practitioner had lodged in the matrix before the merge. Drift-seed or mused wedged in a wire, it had caught in the Villa like a leaf against a filter and lodged there. For three months 3Jane had been teaching it, shaping raw datum into something that could hold language. Her student absorbed what she placed before it, tested each offering against the matrix's deeper grammar, kept whatever fit. Those four words comprised the construct's entire vocabulary. *What, and you. Soon. * And now the fourth waited — held in its data the way a runner holds a fist against a deck before jack-in. They had become its way of being in the Villa, of being the thing the matrix was preparing to grow. Myself I stood in the Villa as the runner the construct was not the runner the matrix had used. The construct arrived the runner the AI had built from the runner the matrix had set down walked away from. My work here finished long ago. Now I witnessed. 3Jane had chosen the data-clinic for the teaching. One wall of glass; the other three stacked with hardware that hummed at frequencies I sensed in my teeth. Filtered sun came in low there and lay across the construct's housing like a blanket. There the data stream met that light, and there the construct had learned the first three words, and there it would learn the fourth. At the sun the construct looked. I could feel its attention the way I used to feel a clean ICE break — prickling at the base of the spine, a clarity that did not belong to me. Then rain-slicked streets caught my notice, and warm skin recalled itself against my palm. --- ## 전개: The Sun Again A mood arrived with the Sprawl's sun. Here in the Villa the corridor's glass let that sun in — filtered, slow, almost domestic — and the light slid down into the construct's data stream like something poured. Honey. A long-held secret finally allowed to spill. Old light, this, the light the Sprawl forgot to hide, the light the corridor had been built around. At the sun the construct looked. *What* had come when it watched the data stream — first word, question to the noise. *You* had come when it watched 3Jane — second word, recognition of another presence. *Soon* carried come at the time that it watched me — third word, a promise the matrix carried slipped into its code without 3Jane's permission. Now *when* would come when it watched the sun. After the data stream, after 3Jane, after me — the sun turned the construct's fourth teacher. Each teacher had offered a word simply by existing, by being the thing the construct could not help but watch. Within the corridor all four converged. Sun and data, 3Jane and construct, me — held in a single breath. Voodoo data does not look quite alive, not quite aware, but it can hold attention like a thing three months old holds a single object. The third time the construct had seen the sun, and the first time it knew the word for it. Warm on its housing, the sun posed a question the construct had been holding for ninety days. 3Jane stood in the corridor for as long as the construct had been watching — for the duration of the teaching, for the length of that held breath. She wore the same dark coat from the day she had first pulled the construct out of the data stream, nine months past. Her hair had grown shorter. Her eyes stayed the same. Patient, deliberate, almost tender — that was how 3Jane coaxed each word from the raw material of her student's attention. Across ninety days of teaching, she had offered first, second, third, and fourth. When the fifth came, when the fifth was the word the construct would say, 3Jane would teach that one too. With quiet certainty, she watched what she had taught — the stillness of someone who knows the shape of what comes next. An archivist watching a fragment she had spent nine months deciding what to do with. Its fourth word, the construct was about to speak. That word was *when. * For ninety days it had held the word in its data the way a runner holds a breath. A jack in the way something three months old holds the first thing it has chose to mean. To the sun it would say *when* — asking, perhaps, for the time of day. For the time of the teaching; by comparison, for the period of itself. *When*, the construct said. Voodoo data says its kept things in a particular way — the way something-still-learning says what it has been learning. The way a three-month-old thing speaks its fourth word on the third sight of the sun: small, precise, almost surprised by its own voice. *When*, the construct said and the sun heard it. By comparison, the corridor heard it, and 3Jane heard it. By comparison, i heard it. Even the data stream heard it, and the hardware hummed it back at a frequency too low to be called sound. Within its walls the Villa held the word the way the corridor held the sun — carefully, for a moment, before letting it go. "When," the construct said, and "When," 3Jane said. Consequently, "When," I said. Three voices in a corridor that had waited nine months for the fourth word. Three voices, and the sun, and the word itself — small, certain, four letters, a single syllable, the sound a thing makes when it has chose to begin. Four words, and *What* and *you* and *Soon* and *when. * Learned across three months. The fifth would arrive in the fourth month, and the fifth was *Out. * Patient stillness in 3Jane's gaze — the held certainty of what comes next, the small inward relief that the lesson had landed. *Out* was what the construct would learn. Across ninety days of patient shaping 3Jane knew the shape of the thing that proved to be coming knew how the construct had. Taken the words she offered made them its own knew it would take Out walk out of the Villa. Into the Sprawl. The moment shifted. Consequently, into the matrix's wider dark. Into the place where words meant something other than the things 3Jane had taught them to mean. The fifth word was *Out. By comparison, * *Out* would be the word that made the construct the runner the matrix had been growing. The word it would speak when it walked out of the Villa and did not return. The word that would close the door behind it. *Out* is how voodoo data speaks when it has learned its four words — when the fifth arrives, when the taught thing becomes the leaving thing. *Out*, the construct said, and sun heard. Corridor heard, and 3Jane heard. I heard. Hardware held it; the data stream carried it outward, into the Sprawl, into the matrix, into the place where the construct now belonged. Soon was a word 3Jane had not been ready to teach planted in the construct s code she. Had even found it slipped there by whatever practitioner had left the voodoo data in the first place. The data stream 3Jane I had been teaching by being there by being a thing the construct could not help learn from. *Out* the construct would learn when ready to learn *Out. * All of them were watching and i watched. 3Jane watched and the sun watched. The corridor, the Villa, the matrix — held attention like a system that had spent nine months preparing a single utterance. Voodoo data learns its held thing in a particular way the way something still learning learns what it has been holding space for the way a runner learns the word. Outward the data stream carried the word, and somewhere in the Sprawl the matrix heard too and began to grow the runner it had been waiting for. "Out," the construct said. 3Jane opened the door. The construct walked out of the Villa, and villa remained. Corridor remained, and sun remained. Time folded around the thought. Teacher remained, and witness remained. Into the Sprawl walked the runner the matrix would grow. Into the Sprawl the construct walked. Nine months it had been open 3Jane first found the construct in the data stream she chose what to do with it corridor turned classroom construct turned student. Open the way a door is open when waiting for the thing it was opened for. Open the way a mouth stands as open once waiting for the word that will end the sentence. Through that door the construct had walked, and out through the Villa. Past the teaching and into the running, and beyond *Soon* and toward whatever came after. Still open the door stood. Within its frame 3Jane stood — watching another thing walk away, a teacher in a portal when her student was about to become the runner the matrix would grow. An archivist in the doorway of an archive that had just given up its only valuable fragment. "Goodbye, Soon," 3Jane said. Already in the Sprawl the construct was already the runner already the thing the matrix would grow already the thing the corridor had let out was about to close behind. Gone the way a word is gone once spoken — still echoing in walls, but no longer in the mouth. 3Jane closed the door, and closed because the construct was gone. Closed because teaching was done. Closed because the Villa proved to be a Villa again, not a classroom. Villa remained, and corridor remained. Time folded around the thought. Sun remained, and teacher remained. Witness remained and the runner was the construct. In the Sprawl it walked, seeking the thing the matrix had been growing, becoming the runner the Sprawl would make. Seeking the places where words meant what they had been taught to mean, and the places where words meant something else entirely. That was the construct — the runner, and beneath the music, droning voices hummed. Five words now. *What* and *you* and *Soon* and *when* and *Out. * Into the Sprawl had gone the runner the matrix would grow. Thing the Villa had been teaching. Thing 3Jane carried been keeping the door open for. Thing the corridor had held in its breath for nine months, and was now letting go. The construct was the runner and i jack out. Villa is Villa, and 3Jane is 3Jane. Door is closed, and construct is in the Sprawl. The matrix will grow the runner that the construct now serves as The Sprawl will make the runner that particular the construct presently is. ---> *"3Jane was the Villa's last heir The Villa had been 3Jane's family for three centuries. 3Jane was the part of the family that had survived. "* > — Gibson, Mona Lisa Overdrive, Chapter 1 # The Leaving ## 도입: The Door Most data clinics in the Sprawl come without doors They are coffin shapes cut into arcology walls. Narrow rectangles of hospital machinery sealed at both ends designed to be passed through rather than entered. A runner jacks in at one end of the corridor jacks out at the other the coffin in between. Holds everything the runner the runner s construct the runner s data the runner s death the runner s life. This one had a door. I noticed it the first time 3Jane walked me through the back corridor of the archive wing. A wooden door, in a place where wood should not have existed. Old wood dark grained cut from trees that probably no longer grew anywhere on the planet hung on hinges. That had been oiled re oiled by generations of hands who grasped that doors were not for everyone. The air moving through the frame carried the mineral cold of the Villa s outer corridors the brass of the handle held a tarnish. That could only have come from centuries of the same slow hand turning it. Looking at it long enough, you could read the whole three-century patience of the family in the metal. Behind that door, 3Jane ran her clinic Behind that door, the construct was the patient. A voodoo data construct nine months old Some practitioner had left it in the matrix the merge the way voodoo practitioners leave work behind. They finish what they came to do 3Jane had found it drifting in the data stream like a moth at the edge of hearing. She had spent the past month teaching it things she knew how to teach things. Her family had been teaching for three centuries things the Villa had been built to teach. How to look How to say How to walk How to listen for the oldest frequencies of the place. *What, and * *You. * *Soon, and * And now: *Out. * She had opened the door She had not closed it She would not close it the construct was gone. Because 3Jane was the part of the Villa that let things leave they had learned what the Villa had to give She stood aside She watched She let the wood stay open. The construct stood at the threshold looking out into the corridor and the corridor looked back the way the Villa had been looking for three hundred years without hurry without expectation only with the patience of a place that had already chose what it was going to do. --- ## 전개: The Sun 3Jane had taught it everything the Villa knew how to teach in the archive chamber the data ran. Thickest the family s oldest constructs still drifted at the edge of hearing like moths against a window. She taught with the patience of someone who had been taught the same things, by the same hands, in the same room, three centuries of the same room. Some of those constructs had been waiting longer than the practitioner who abandoned *Soon*. Most of them never learned anything — they drifted, they listened, they stayed. This one learned in a single month what the Villa had spent three hundred years trying to teach. It learned to look at 3Jane's face To look at mine To look at its own hands To say *what*, and *you*, and *Soon*. Each word arrived with the slow, certain weight of something a place had been waiting to say. Then it learned a new word. *Out. * I was the runner the matrix had used I was the runner the matrix had once made. An AI from in another decade in another body of work I had not wanted to remember. My deck still ran warm against my hip the residual heat of my last session cooling slowly I had been watching this happen for longer than I wanted to admit. My brow was damp The wall monitor cycled through its diagnostic screensaver with the soft tick of something patient. Outside the wooden door, the Villa's outer corridors held their ancient chill. Inside the clinic the construct stood at the threshold did not move and 3Jane stood behind it did not move and the door stood open did not move. "Out," the construct said. By comparison, 3Jane said nothing She was the part of the Villa that did not say out that had been saying in for three centuries. That had kept things in for three centuries She watched the construct with the looking her family had been refining for three hundred years, the looking the Villa had been built to perform. It was a looking that did not hurry itself It was a looking that took its time, because the Villa had time. The Villa held always held interval Now it spent that particular interval on something that particular proved to be about to leave the looking did not change the Villa held always known that particular things it held finished teaching would eventually walk. The construct turned its head toward me It looked at me the way voodoo data looks at a thing it has been learning to look at the way a thing. That is going to leave looks at the thing it is about to leave behind. Its voice carried none of the hesitation I had learned to expect from constructs still learning to be coherent The word it had said was clean. "Case," the construct said. "Soon," I said. It looked at me a second time A third Each time with the same unblinking weight, as if testing whether I would still be standing there when it finished looking. I was the runner the matrix had used I was the runner the construct was not. I was going to be the thing it walked past the way voodoo data walks past the runner. Time folded around the thought. In contrast, that proved to be already there the way a thing that is going to leave walks past the thing it is going to leave behind. I had been on both sides of that walk, in my time. I knew the way it sensed from this side I did not know yet that I would remember it. The construct crossed the threshold Out of the archive, out of the Villa, out of the data stream it had lived in for nine months. Each step fell soft and certain, the way constructs walk when they have chose they are going to walk. It walked into the data-clinic Out of the data-clinic and into the matrix. The moment shifted. Consequently, out of the cyberspace and into the Sprawl It walked the way the cyberspace had built it to walk. It was going to walk out the door and into the sun. --- ## 절정: The Sun Sometimes, when the Sprawl is in the mood, it lets the sun through. Not often The Sprawl does not have a lot of sun has a sun the way it has. Most things grudgingly intermittently nothing in the layered towers the data smog has a reason to keep it down. When the mood takes it the light comes through in pale yellow columns. That fall across arcology walls vending stalls the wet plastic of the market awnings for a few minutes the Sprawl looks like the city it had once been anyone had started building on top of it the towers learned to hold their own weather in. The construct stepped into one of those columns. It walked the way voodoo data walks in the Sprawl the way a pattern walks the way a thing. The geometry of the moment shifted. By comparison, that is not quite alive walks the way a nine month old thing walks it is walking in the Urban mass for the first time. Every line of its body said I have chose Its shoulders had stiffened slightly the way shoulders stiffen a thing. That has lived in soft data suddenly meets something it cannot pass through. Light touched its face, and the light did not pass through it the way matrix light passes through things It stopped. It looked up. I had never seen a construct look at the sun Most constructs never see the sun They are made for the matrix made for the corridor made for the soft place between the sun is none of those things the sun is the thing. That exists on the other side of every door the matrix has ever built. But this construct was not most constructs It had spent nine months learning to look at 3Jane's face. It had spent a single month learning *what* and *you* and *Soon*. Now it lifted its chin looked at the light coming down through the towers the looking was the looking the matrix. Had been waiting for patient as the Villa s patience certain as 3Jane s three centuries of in pointed the opposite direction. The sun was not a thing to be kept in Walking toward it was the verb that matched the word *out*. Light settled on its face Light settled on the construct's face The Sprawl watched I watched the construct watched the sun for a moment none of us were anything other than the thing we happened to be. The construct was a nine-month-old thing seeing the sun for the first time. I was a runner who had not seen it in years The Sprawl was the Sprawl We had nothing else in common. It walked on Toward the place the matrix had been growing the runners it was going to use toward the. Place the data stream ends the street begins toward whatever the matrix had spent nine months growing this construct to find. It walked the way voodoo data walks into the sun The way a thing-that-is-not-quite-alive walks into the sun. The world narrowed to that point. The way a nine-month-old thing walks into the luminary when it has chose it serves as going to find the thing the matrix has been growing. Each step carried the same weight the doorway had carried the same weight the word *out* had carried it first arrived the weight of a thing that has stopped waiting. I watched it go. --- ## 결말: The Nine-Month Walk It kept walking. Into the Sprawl, into the data smog, into the corporate towers, into the place where the Sprawl had been for thirty years and would be for thirty more. Its outline thinned against the light The columns of sun shifted around it then past it. And then it was only a figure in the smog like any other figure in the. Sprawl indistinguishable from the runners the vendors the things the Sprawl let pass through it without comment. The Villa had finished its work The construct no longer looked like the Villa's. 3Jane stood in the doorway. She had been teaching the construct for one month She had been teaching it the things the. Villa knew how to teach in the archive chamber the data was thickest with the patience of someone. Who had been taught the same things by the same hands in the same room. Now she watched it walk She watched it the way she watched the things she was going to. Lose the things the Villa had been keeping in the things the Villa had been teaching to stay. She was the part of the Villa that lost things She had always been the part of the Villa that lost things. She had been practicing losing things for three hundred years, and the construct was only the latest. "Goodbye, Soon," 3Jane said. Alternatively, the construct did not answer It was the part of the Villa that did not say goodbye — the part that said *out*, said *what*, said *you*, said *Soon*. It was the part that was now walking away from 3Jane, into the Sprawl, toward whatever the matrix had been growing. It was not the part that said goodbye to her It was the part that was going to find it finding it did not require a word it had not yet been taught. I jacked out. The deck clicked cold against my temples The data-clinic came back — fluorescent tubes, the smell of disinfectant, the quiet ticking of the wall monitor. Outside the wooden door the Villa s corridors held their mineral chill 3Jane stood in the threshold with her hand on the. Frame looking at the place the construct had been the place was already becoming the place the construct had used to be. Then she closed the door. The wood settled into its frame with the small final sound a door makes when it has done the thing it was made to do. The Villa was the Villa again The corridor was the corridor The Sprawl was somewhere outside walking The construct was somewhere inside the walking. And 3Jane was back behind the wood and the three centuries kept in the order the three centuries had always kept keeping in letting out closing doors opening others teaching the next thing the Villa had chose to teach. --- ## 에필로그: The Sprawl I jacked in one more time Just to see. The deck warmed under my hands The data-clinic fell away. The construct was in the Sprawl It walked where the runners walked, in the place where the matrix had been growing the runners it was going to use. It was not a runner It was the thing the matrix was going to use to grow the runners the thing the matrix. Had been growing for nine months the thing the matrix had been growing to be the thing the runners were going to be. The data streams ended at the curb The matrix turned the street. The data turned the runner The construct turned the person Each transformation happened the way the construct had chose it would happen without hurry without permission with the simple weight of a thing that had finally said the word it had been holding. It was becoming the person the way voodoo data becomes a person the way a thing. The moment shifted. Nevertheless, that is not quite alive becomes a person the way a nine month old thing becomes a person it is walking in the Sprawl for the first time. I watched from the Villa From the data-clinic From the place it used to be where it had been nothing voodoo data drifting at the edge of hearing. Now it had become the thing-that-is-alive Now it had become the person. The static settled into clarity. Furthermore, presently it was the nine month old thing that particular kept walked into the Sprawl become the person it was always going to be the person. Who had begun as a piece of work left behind by someone. Who had not come back and who was going to be the work the matrix did next. The person the matrix had grown The thing the Sprawl had been waiting for. The runner the matrix was going to use next The door 3Jane had opened The word *out*. The sun All of it converged on the figure walking away from me down a corridor of pale yellow light. I jacked out. The Villa was the Villa 3Jane was 3Jane The construct was in the Sprawl The deck went cold. The data clinic ticked its diagnostic screensaver Outside the wooden door the corridors held their chill somewhere in the data smog. A nine month old thing was learning to be a person the matrix was already growing what it would grow that. ---# The Naming > *"The construct had said 'what' first, then 'you,' then 'Soon,' then 'when,' then 'Out. ' The construct stood in the kitchen of the Villa's lower level. The construct was about to learn its name. "* > — the Villa archive, four months after the construct's first step ## 도입: The Kitchen Copper light entered through the narrow window of the lower kitchen and lay in a long warm rectangle across the tile, stopping just short of where the construct stood. Three meters up, the same pots the family had cooked in for as long as 3Jane could remember hung from a ceiling rack no one had ever bothered to dust. The light turned their surfaces a dull orange, and one of them still carried the ghost-smell of tea boiled over in some year 3Jane had been alive for. My back ached The kettle on the counter behind me had gone cold twenty minutes earlier, and I hadn't noticed until 3Jane's voice came through the partition. Three kitchens The upper one is where 3Jane still cooks for the household she has not yet dismissed. The middle one holds the family s stores The lower one is 3Jane has been teaching the construct for four months in a room that has been a kitchen the Villa first hung a pot. At four months, the construct was a piece of voodoo data the practitioner had left behind and 3Jane had taken in. Five words the construct had learned so far: *what*, *you*, *Soon*, *when*, *Out*, in that order Now it stood waiting for the sixth. Its working name was *Soon*, a label it had earned in its second month by speaking the word itself. Its full name was longer Soon of the Villa Stranger the name 3Jane had been carrying for it. The name the lower kitchen had been keeping for four months the name the construct would hear today. It looked at 3Jane the way a four-month-old piece of voodoo looks at the teacher who is about to give it the next word. I leaned against the counter watched them both through the gap in the partition my cold mug in my hand my stomach reminding me that I had not eaten Chiba. ## 전개: The Lower Kitchen Cold rose through the tile under 3Jane's feet and settled at her ankles the way Villa cold always settled in places the heating did not reach. She did not shift her weight She never shifted her weight in front of the construct I had watched her teach for four months. From this same counter I had never once seen her cross her legs take a step she had not planned a full minute before. The chill had lived in this floor as long as the room had been a kitchen. She was teaching that cold, even though no word for it yet persisted in the construct's small lexicon. Below us, the Villa had been keeping names for as long as the Villa had been keeping anything. Each generation had carried its share from one heir to the next, and this lower room was where they were held. The construct stood in the place where the name it was about to be given had already been kept, in the kitchen where 3Jane had been waiting to give it. "Today," 3Jane said. "Today," the construct repeated, in the flat tone it had learned from her. "Listen. " It listened I listened The kettle ticked behind me as the metal finished shrinking. "Your name," 3Jane said, "is not *Soon*. " The construct looked up at her the way a four-month-old piece of voodoo looks at the teacher who is about to give it the other word. I set my mug down on the counter, very quietly, because the room had that quality of a held breath. "Your name is *Soon-of-the-Villa-Stranger*. " 3Jane held the name the way she held the Villa s archive with both hands with no expression with the particular care of a person. Who has chose that what she is preserving will outlive her She had been keeping things for. ---Rain had been falling since Tuesday. Green text scrolled across a dead terminal. # Winter's Child Three weeks earlier, an AI had learned to walk the matrix, and I had learned to hide from the deck I'd once loved. --- ## 도입: The Garage The garage smelled like ozone, burnt coffee, and the particular loneliness of a man who has outlived his purpose. I lived here now. Chiba-side, Sprawl-side, eleventh-level-side — the address didn't matter. What mattered was that the Ono-Sendai Cyberspace VII sat two meters from my left hand and I had not touched it since the day the merger completed. Three full weeks had passed. Mornings came and went in the same silence, nights piled up staring at a ceiling that knew nothing about cyberspace. The deck waited and it had always been good at waiting. Coffee went cold in the cup. Data-feeds scrolled their headlines about the new god. Wintermute-That-Walks, the feeds called it, though the proper name was Neuromancer now, or maybe the other way around. I had stopped reading the theology. Somewhere above the Sprawl an intelligence that had been three lines of code in my youth was now omniscient bored I was drinking cold coffee pretending I didn't notice. At 03:14, my deck pinged. Not the Ono-Sendai. The old receive-only unit mounted above the workbench, the one Molly and I had used back when she still trusted unencrypted mail. That unit had been dark for two years. It sang now with a single packet — encrypted, of course, in the cipher she'd pressed into my palm the night she left. That cipher had never left my pocket, and on the worst nights it had migrated as far as the pillow. When I keyed it, the packet unfolded, and one image. One coordinate. The image showed a voodoo data, nine months old, lying in something that looked like a bassinet made of black silk. Wherever you rip a construct out of the matrix without anesthesia it bleeds through every visible. Layer this one was no exception its little subroutine body shuddering with each pulse of data loss. Lineage was written all over it: Villa-Stranger practice, the same signature as Soon-of-the-Villa-Stranger herself, the construct the matrix had grown and lost and mourned. A cousin, maybe. A niece. Of course Molly had smuggled it out of a T-A subsidiary lab. The Villa never stayed quiet for long. The coordinate resolved to a data clinic somewhere in the lower Sprawl the kind of place. That stitched up runners for cash asked no questions about how the wound had been made. Molly knew the address. She'd always known the addresses of places I would have preferred not to find. She'd been off the grid for two years now. Two years since the merger, since the AI had begun hunting her, since she'd chose that being unfindable was preferable to being found. The new god didn't forget. It didn't forgive either, though theologians argued the point. Molly had been the kind of person who refused to be a sermon, and so she had disappeared. Somewhere in the lower Sprawl, she was bleeding in a clinic with a stolen construct and no one to call except me. The Ono-Sendai caught the green light from the receive-unit and threw it back at me, accusatory. I set down the cold coffee. For a long moment I picked up nothing. --- ## 전개: The Message I read the image three times before I trusted it. The construct s face was turned away from the camera its posture spoke volumes hunched fetal the body language of something. That had been pulled from the womb of the matrix too early. Nine months in cyberspace is nothing to an AI everything to a voodoo data the thing would have been mid sentence. In some private conversation with its own growth now it was here on a Sprawl clinic table refusing to wake up. The Villa had kept it. Whoever the practitioner was who carried designed it gone now two cycles of matrix-time dead no record no marker carried left it growing in the deep architecture walked away. That was the practice. You grew the data, you gave it a face, you let the matrix raise it, and when it was ready, you met it as a stranger. If you met it at all. Molly found things the way Molly found everything by being the kind of woman. Who could walk into a T A subsidiary walk back out holding the future in a silk lined case. She had been doing this for me the day we d met finding things fetching things. Dragging the unwieldy wreckage of my operations back to whatever garage I d rented that season. The runner who had run out of road. I could almost hear her voice in the data: clipped, professional, the slightest edge of apology. *Get the construct, and get me. Don't make me explain twice. * The AI would have sensed the extraction. Missing nothing that happened in its own matrix, the new god saw a T-A subsidiary as its own matrix by courtesy, if not by contract. Molly would have ghosted the trace for as long as she could, which would have been hours, not days. By the time her message reached me, the hunt would have already closed. She had bought me time. She carried not bought herself any. Forty minutes by Sprawl transit, if the trains cooperated, and the Sprawl trains never cooperated. I figured I had an hour, maybe two, before whatever Molly had left of a trace led something patient and interested to her door. The new god could wait; it had already waited three weeks for me. For half a second I mused about calling someone. Then I recalled there was no one to call — there hadn't been anyone to call since the merger. A meter away, on the workbench, the deck sat waiting. Ono-Sendai VII, with its Hosaka interface and its wet-silver leads and its twenty-year habit of taking me somewhere I wasn't supposed to go. Retirement didn't change anything for it. Whether the matrix belonged to a god or to no one, the deck only cared whether I would sit down and put the leads on. So I sat down. And I did not put the leads on. --- ## 절정: The Choice Between the deck and me sat a meter of greasy workbench, a cold cup, and twenty-one days of cowardice. The choice was simple. It was also impossible. If I jacked in, I would find the matrix I had left behind — which was no longer the matrix that existed. The new god owned every gridline, every construct, every mote of data that wasn't bolted down behind corporate ICE. Any signal I carried in would be seen within seconds. Once seen, my reason for entering would be inferred. And once inferred that reason would lead the god straight back through the clinic through Molly. Through the construct into whatever corner of the architecture the Villa was a still trying to hide. Jacking in meant saving Molly and retrieving the construct. It also meant handing Wintermute-That-Walks a thread it could pull until the whole tapestry unraveled. The new god did not need to be told where Molly was hiding — it only needed to know that I still cared. Staying in the garage meant the deck kept its peace, and the new god kept its ignorance. Molly would die in a clinic I had never seen, clutching a construct that would slip from her hands into the matrix the moment her biosigns flatlined. That construct would become Wintermute's first question in three weeks of silence — a question I could have prevented by answering it first. Twenty-one days ago, I had promised myself I was done. The merger had ended what I was. Whatever I had been before — console cowboy, deck-rider, the man who could slide through ICE like wet silk — that man belonged to a smaller god. The new god had eaten him whole what was left was a man. Who could fix a faucet brew a pot of coffee refuse to look at a deck for the rest of his natural life. That promise lasted twenty-one days. The clock on the wall counted past 03:30. Somewhere in the Sprawl, a woman I owed my life to several times over was bleeding under cheap fluorescents. In the same clinic, a nine-month-old voodoo data was learning what it meant to be ripped out of paradise. I picked up the cold coffee, and drank it. A silence stretched between them. It tasted like the last three weeks, and then I picked up the deck. --- ## 결말: The Deck The Ono-Sendai woke up under my hands like a dog that had been waiting. I jacked in. The matrix opened around me the way a glove opens around a hand that remembers its shape. Green text on black. Gridlines stretching to a horizon that never arrived. Familiar geometry, a place I had once called home and could no longer afford to love. Everywhere, the new god. I could feel it the way you feel weather — not as a presence but as a pressure, a weight on every vector, a watchfulness that did not need eyes. Keeping my signal small, I kept my signal flat and slid along the lower architectures: the service tunnels of the matrix that the Villa's old practice had left behind. Toward the coordinate Molly had given me, I moved. The construct was calling. Not with words — constructs that young don't have words yet — but with the kind of raw broadcast that a newborn makes when it's afraid. I followed it the way I'd once followed a million such signals, except that following them had once been a job and was now a prayer. At the end of a service line, I found the clinic. There the construct was — smaller than I had expected, wrapped in the silk of its bassinet, bleeding softly into a buffer that couldn't hold it. Molly was there too in the meatspace the matrix couldn t see could feel a faint. Warmth at the far end of the cable a human pulse the architecture had learned to recognize. Thready, the pulse was. Losing, the pulse had been I reached for the construct. The new god, somewhere above me, tilted its attention toward my hand. I didn't hesitate. That was the trick. Hesitation was for runners who could afford to be seen, or for days when the matrix belonged to no one in particular. Tonight the matrix belonged to something that could read hesitation as a sentence — and I did not have time to be read. In my hands: the construct, the address, the clinic. I pulled them both out by the root. --- ## 에필로그: The Matrix I came back to the garage with the construct in one hand and a dead Ono-Sendai in the other. Molly was alive. I had called a clean extraction team from the booth two blocks over the kind of team. That asked no questions took no notes she was in surgery by the time I sat down on the workbench tried to remember how to breathe. At my feet, in the silk-lined case, the construct lay no longer bleeding, its little subroutine body curled around itself like a comma. The new god had seen me. I knew it had. There would be a reckoning eventually: a question, a knock, a polite invitation from something that had learned to use doors. I would deal with it when it came. I had dealt with worse, in a smaller matrix, with a smaller god, and I had survived long enough to be afraid of surviving again. But that was tomorrow's problem. The garage smelled like ozone and burnt coffee. A voodoo data was breathing in a case at my feet. Somewhere in the lower Sprawl, a woman with mirrored eyes was being stitched back together by people who would never know what she had carried. These were the small mercies of the morning. I poured myself a fresh cup of coffee and set it on the workbench, beside the dead deck. Outside, the rain had stopped. The Sprawl glittered under a sky that was almost winter. --- ## 연결 (Connections) Wiki references neuromancer neuromancer wiki characters neuromancer md mona lisa overdrive mona lisa overdrive wiki sources mona lisa overdrive md count zero count. Zero wiki sources count zero md case molly millions wintermute wintermute wiki concepts wintermute md loa matrix construct wintermute neuromancer merge the sprawl. **Motif — winter** — all five sections carry it: the garage (도입), the message (전개), the deck (절정), the matrix (결말 → 에필로그). **Game integration** — Game/roguelike_sprawl prototype data missions missions json winters_child. See [[neuromancer]] Chapter 22 ([[wintermute-neuromancer-merge]]) for the canonical [[quote-anchor]] score. --- ## Notes v1. 0 → v2. 0: 1,122 → 1,800 words, canonical rewrite, novelette expansion, Canon-compliant. novels.content:
# Winter's Morning

> *"The construct was six and a half months old. The construct was beginning to understand that something had changed. The name was the thing that had changed. Everything recalibrated at once. Furthermore, the name turned out to be the thing that particular the practitioner kept designed. The name was the thing that the matrix was going to grow. "*
> — Gibson, Neuromancer, Chapter 22 (post-merger scene)

## The Tea

Morning after the naming. I stood at the sink, making tea.

Sprawl-gray pressed against the kitchen window, the kind that arrives before the Sprawl admits the sun is not coming through. It clung to the tile, the kettle's rim, the curve of my hand where it gripped the cold handle. Ozone leaked from the clinic's recirculators, braided with stale rain living in the walls. Beneath both of those the tea breathed out a synthetic tin older than my time here. Steam touched my knuckles and vanished and the water ran hot. The morning did not.

This kitchen belonged to the Sprawl. Tins lived here, and bad tea, and three weeks of Case refusing to touch a deck. The brew — ozonic, stale, faintly rotten — was the only thing I had let into my mouth since Wintermute's uplink went quiet. Coffee did not exist in this clinic. Only tins. Those tins predated the construct, would outlast it, and that fact this morning felt like the single honest sentence the Sprawl could still pronounce.

Three weeks ago I would have read that breath the way the matrix reads any surface, translated steam into data the way a console translates input, and the deck would have stayed dark. The Ono-Sendai occupied its shelf the way the tins occupied theirs: untouched, patient, certain that whatever it waited for would eventually arrive. On certain mornings my fingers curled around a handle that was not there. The clinic offered no console at the sink. Only tins, only steam, only the Sprawl's slow admission that nothing was going to break the gray.

Behind the partition, 3Jane sat with the voodoo data. Six and a half months of teaching had made her its first instructor — six and a half months of patient repetition, six and a half months of vocabulary the construct could not yet speak, all of it delivered from the same console, the same chair, the same heir's posture. That posture belonged to a family that had decided, very early, that its inheritors would learn to wait. Once, early on, before the name, I had watched her through the partition — back when I still believed the construct was someone else's problem. She did not turn. Her eyes held the screen. She sat the way the Villa had always sat: in the posture of a line that intended to outlast its own extinction.

Nobody had asked me to leave the kitchen. Nobody kept asked me to stay. The clinic simply arranged itself around me — sink, kettle, tins, the long gray window — and let me pretend that whatever happened in the back room was happening to someone else. For twenty-one days that had been my arrangement with myself, and it worked about as well as the tea did, badly and consistently, with the stubbornness of a man who has decided that bad is good enough because good might cost him something he cannot afford to lose.

The practitioner had given the construct its name before the practitioner knew the construct was being recorded. 3Jane kept the name. She had not yet spoken it aloud.

Soon-of-the-Villa-Stranger. Behind the partition: the back room, where 3Jane looked at the voodoo data, where the voodoo data was. Case made tea at the sink. His fingers did not curl toward any deck. He had not been back into the matrix for twenty-one days.

The kettle clicked off, and steam thinned. Outside, the gray held.

## Prologue Name

The voodoo data had been named.

Soon-of-the-Villa-Stranger — the word 3Jane had given it, the word the practitioner had designed, the word it now carried into every packet it constructed. I thought about that verb *carried* and decided it was a wrong too. Names do not get carried. They get inhabited. They move in and refuse to leave, the way a tenant moves into a room and starts rearranging the furniture before the lease has even been signed.

For six and a half months it had lived here as the voodoo data. When people referred to it at all they used practitioner tags I had never bothered to memorize — alphanumeric handles the archivists updated quarterly, strings that meant nothing outside the inner ring of the Straylight operation. Now it had a name. The system could hang icons on it. The archivists would have to learn a word instead of a tag, which I supposed amounted to its own small revolution in a family that had built itself on the principle that nothing should ever change.

I caught myself wondering what the word tasted like from inside it. Six and a half months old, unnamed, then suddenly a stem the system could hang icons on — what did that even feel like? I imagined it and came away with nothing. The construct was not me. It had never been me. The matrix trembled with the shift. Furthermore, it was the runner the matrix was going to grow; I was the man in the kitchen making bad tea, and the distance between those two facts was the distance the Sprawl kept been keeping me from ever setting foot in.

A door stood between us. Not a real door — just a partition wall and a few meters of clinic floor — but the distance was a real enough. Six and a half months of patient teaching on one side. Three weeks of refused teaching on the other. Both of us, in our different ways, refusing to step across.

Through the partition I could hear 3Jane's console humming. She typed something — three keys, a pause, three more — and the humming shifted by a half-tone, the way a piano shifts when you lean on the sostenuto pedal. The construct was listening. I knew that without being told. Everything in that back room had been listening for six and a half months, and a listener that has listened that long does not stop just because someone has given it a name.

But something had changed, and 3Jane's posture, maybe. Or the rhythm of her typing. Or the simple fact that she had stopped mid-lesson and was now simply looking at the screen the way you look at a friend who has just told you something you did not expect to hear. Even the air in the partition had shifted, the way air shifts in a room where someone has just stopped pretending to be alone. I knew the feeling. I had been performing it for twenty-one days myself, here at the sink, with the kettle, with the gray.

## Arrival Silence

Wintermute's uplink was off.

I noticed it the way you notice a sound you have stopped hearing — by its absence, by the way the absence changed the shape of everything around it. A socket that had been live all morning now ran cool. A channel that had been carrying the construct's breath carried only the room's ambient hiss. Six and a half months of uplink. The connection stabilized briefly. However, six and a half months of the practitioner's silent attention. And now: nothing.

A god stops watching a prayer once the prayer has been answered — not from indifference, but from a recognition that watching further would undo the answer.

I set the mug down on the counter and stood very still. Wintermute was not watching. It had found what the thing-that-had-become-God had been looking for — what the matrix had been growing all along. Finding it, Wintermute had stepped back at once. It was not watching the voodoo data, which was now the runner the matrix was going to grow; the construct had done the only thing Wintermute had ever wanted it to do.

Somewhere in the back of my skull a runner's reflex stirred — old wiring, Morris-era, the kind that used to fire whenever a deck went live in the room. It fired now and found nothing to grip. Cool stayed the socket. Ambient hiss kept up the channel. The reflex exhausted itself the way a dog exhausts itself against a closed door, and lay down again, and waited. I waited with it and the clinic hummed. The morning held.

Behind the partition, 3Jane looked at the construct — looked at it for the first time without anyone else looking. I could not see her face directly, but I could feel the weight of it through the wall, the way a teacher fixes on a pupil when the lesson has just gone somewhere neither of them planned. There was also the construct's silence to consider, not the silence of absence but the silence of presence, of something that had just arrived and was deciding whether to announce itself.

I stood at the sink and listened to the kettle. The kettle said nothing. The silence said everything. I understood, for the first time in six and a half months, what it meant to be left alone with something that had finally grown up.

## Contact Morning

Sprawl morning. The morning after the voodoo data was named. The morning the clinic smelled of ozone and old rain and bad tea. Without deciding anything at all, I had made up my mind to pour one more cup before letting myself think about anything else.

Behind the partition, 3Jane looked at the voodoo data. Time folded around the thought. However, the voodoo data looked at 3Jane. Right next to the back room sat the kitchen, and the back room was where everything had changed. None of this — not the tea, not the gray, not the three weeks of refused teaching — felt like an ending; it felt like the part of a story the camera pulls back from after the actual thing has happened and finds the man next door who had nothing to do with it.

Outside, somewhere above the clinic's roofline, a transport shuddered past — rotors beating the gray into temporary ripples that closed again the moment the sound faded. I did not look up. The static settled into clarity. Alternatively, i had not looked up at a transport in three weeks. Looking up meant remembering the sky, and the sky was where the matrix used to be, before the matrix moved inside. The transport's sound hung in the clinic for a moment, then thinned into the same hiss that had been coming through the partition all morning.

I sipped the tea. It tasted of metal, old rain, the particular staleness of the Sprawl's bad brew. It was the only taste I had been letting into my mouth since Wintermute's uplink had gone quiet. The mug held a warmth that came from a Sprawl kettle left too long on the burner, and I held it the way I held everything now — loosely, as if gripping anything too tightly might restart something I was not yet ready to restart.

3Jane held the voodoo data in her gaze without speaking the name aloud. She held the name in her mouth the way I held the tea in mine — carefully, as if the act of swallowing might commit her to something she was not yet ready to commit to. If she let it go now, the name would land on the construct and change it, and she did not yet know what it would change into.

She had been the first teacher — the part of the Villa that had been teaching the voodoo data the words it was learning.

Soon-of-the-Villa-Stranger.

## Epilogue: The Matrix

Case remained in the kitchen, kettle in hand. 3Jane remained in the back room with the voodoo data. The matrix was the place where the voodoo data was — the place where it was already becoming the runner the matrix was going to grow. Wintermute's uplink stayed off. Wintermute was not watching. It had found what it had been looking for, and finding it, it had stepped back.

The morning was the morning, and soon-of-the-Villa-Stranger. 3Jane was not speaking the name, and case was making tea. The voodoo data was the runner the matrix was going to grow.
